The Battle of Trafalgar was a fleet action fought on 21 October 1805 off Cape Trafalgar between the Royal Navy and a combined fleet of the French and Spanish navies during the Trafalgar campaign of the War of the Third Coalition. A Franco-Spanish fleet under French Vice-admiral Pierre-Charles Villeneuve sailed from Cádiz on 18 October 1805 and three days later encountered a British fleet under Vice-Admiral of the White Horatio Nelson, 1st Viscount Nelson in the Atlantic along southwestern Spain.
Nelson sailed his fleet directly at the Franco-Spanish line of battle's flank in two columns, hoping to break the line into pieces. Villeneuve foresaw Nelson's tactic but failed to prepare for it; the crews of the French and Spanish ships in contrast to their British counterparts were inexperienced, poorly trained and suffered from low morale. Nelson's plan worked brilliantly with both columns splitting the Franco-Spanish fleet in three groups, isolating the rear. The Franco-Spanish vanguard sailed ahead while attempting to turn back, leaving the British temporarily superior in number against the remainder of Villeneuve's fleet.

Some favored the abolition of slavery, while others deemed abolition as impractical at that time.
